title: Chapter 14: Missing Persons Notice
html:
At 4:30 p.m., Chen Ge stood alone in the Haunted House’s props room, studying the shelves of equipment with a thoughtful expression.

What should I take for an overnight mission in a dangerous place?

ID, phone, charger, flashlight, water… Right, I can’t forget the doll either.Chen Ge tucked the doll that had appeared in front of the mirror the previous night into his bag. After checking that he had everything he needed, he zipped the bag shut and left the room.

“Xiao Wan, you can leave early today. Remember to lock up when you go. I have something to take care of, so I’m heading out first.”

“Boss, it’s only 5:00 p.m. Are you going on a trip or something?”

“I left the key on the table in the props room. See you tomorrow morning.”

Realizing that Chen Ge was deliberately changing the subject, Xu Wan could only reply, “Okay.”

But the moment Chen Ge turned away, she dropped the Haunted House flyers and darted toward the props room.

“That girl…” The evening breeze stirred the flyers left on the table. Sighing, Chen Ge picked up a pebble and placed it on top of them.Hopefully she won’t be seeing me on the morning news.

Despite his calm appearance, Chen Ge’s thoughts were a mess. The previous night’s Nightmare Mission had opened an entirely new world to him and shown him that the black phone’s missions carried very real risks.

A Trial Mission has to be harder than a Daily Mission. I need to be extra careful tonight.

Before nightfall, Chen Ge set out for Ping An Apartments on his bicycle. The mission details gave him only the location name, so he relied on a map and the complaint posted online nine months earlier. Even then, it took him nearly two hours to find the place.

Do people actually choose to live somewhere this remote and isolated?

The road leading to the apartments twisted through overgrown brush. There were no streetlights, and through gaps in the branches Chen Ge occasionally caught sight of a gray building.

Along the way, Chen Ge stopped to ask everyone he encountered for directions, but most had never heard of Ping An Apartments. Eventually, an older man in his sixties pointed him toward the correct road and offered a friendly warning: the place had a reputation for being haunted and cursed, and most locals avoided it even during the day.

Chen Ge had no answer to that. If not for the black phone’s mission, who would willingly spend the night in a place like this?

It’s only 6:50 p.m., and the mission says I have to arrive before 11:00. I still have plenty of time to look around.Following the winding road deeper into the woods, Chen Ge eventually caught his first clear sight of the supposedly cursed property.

A tall gray wall surrounded the yard, leaving the main gate as the only entrance. The two-leaf iron gate was rusty with age, but the lock hanging from it looked brand-new.

Strange. The gate is old, but the lock is new. Wait—what’s that?A sheet of white paper had been fastened to the iron bars. Chen Ge first took it for a flyer, but when he shone his flashlight over it, he realized it was a missing-person notice.

“Zhang Qing, female, twenty-seven years old, 157 centimeters tall, slim build. Beauty mark beneath the right eye. Often wears red clothing. If you have any information, please contact Mr. Wang. Reward offered!”

The notice included Mr. Wang’s phone number and address. What caught Chen Ge’s attention was that the listed address was the same as this supposedly cursed apartment complex.

“That’s strange.” Chen Ge’s supernatural instincts began to tingle. He photographed the notice with his phone before entering the compound. The property was larger than he had expected: the main building had three stories, with two smaller structures nearby that appeared to be a storage shed and a pump room.

Judging by the peeling paint, this place has to be at least twenty or thirty years old.Despite its age, however, the property was surprisingly well kept. There was no litter, the grounds were clean, and even the lawn had been carefully mowed.

After leaving his bicycle on the lawn, Chen Ge entered the main building with his backpack. “Hello? Is anyone here?”

The long corridor lay in shadow. About ten seconds later, the door closest to the staircase opened a crack.

“Good afternoon.” Chen Ge approached, but the person inside did not seem particularly welcoming; the door stopped after opening only a sliver. The room beyond was dark, and he could barely make out a woman standing behind it. Her eyes were bloodshot and she looked exhausted, as though she had not slept properly in days.

“I wanted to ask how much it costs to stay here for one night,” Chen Ge said as gently as he could. To his surprise, the only response was a quiet giggle before the door slammed shut in his face.

“Huh?” Before he could process what had happened, footsteps sounded on the second floor. The corridor’s only motion-activated light flickered on, revealing a limping middle-aged man descending the stairs.

The man seemed to have overheard him, because his first question was, “You want to stay here? How long?”

“You’re the landlord?” Chen Ge stepped closer. “I only need a room for one night.”

“Just one night?” The limping man looked Chen Ge up and down as though trying to read his intentions. “Fine. Give me your ID. You can pay upstairs.”

Chen Ge was about to follow him when a loud clang came from outside, as though the iron gate had been thrown open. The limping man frowned, his expression tightening with irritation, and stopped on the stairs. A moment later, another middle-aged man entered. He looked exhausted, wore old and tattered clothes, and carried a thick stack of papers.

“Wang Qi, how many times have I told you? Your girlfriend isn’t here! If you keep this up, I’m calling the police!” The limping man planted himself in the middle of the staircase to block the way.

The other man ignored him and continued upstairs with his head lowered.

“Hey, I’m talking to you!” The limping man shoved him aside. Caught off guard, Wang Qi stumbled against the wall, and the stack of papers slipped from his hands and scattered across the stairs. One sheet landed near Chen Ge’s feet.

It’s the same missing-person notice I saw outside,Chen Ge thought, narrowing his eyes. He silently picked up the page and continued watching the confrontation.

Wang Qi did not retaliate. He slowly pushed himself upright and began gathering the notices scattered across the floor without saying a word. His heavy, mechanical movements reminded Chen Ge of a lifeless zombie.

“Don’t mind him. The man’s crazy.” The limping landlord waved for Chen Ge to follow him upstairs. Apparently, he had given up trying to stop Wang Qi.

Crazy?As Chen Ge passed Wang Qi, he stole a discreet glance at him. The mission did mention a dangerous patient. Could this be the person I’m looking for?
